text: Every lesson in this chapter has arrived at the same requirement: verify the draft. "It sounds right" measures fluency, not accuracy.
The simplest technique: sample the AI's output and check it by hand against data you know is correct. If the sample has errors, the full output probably does too.
A second LLM call can evaluate the first one's output and scales further — but the judge shares the exact same blind spots as the model being judged.
Use LLM-as-judge as a fast first filter across a large volume of output, then spot-check a sample of what passes against real ground truth.
Fluency was never the check — a real comparison against ground truth is. Next up: a full worked example of AI-assisted debugging.
